subject: Request: onboarding Polaris-XS variant + temporary pin for streaming latency regression
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@polaris.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: onboarding Polaris-XS variant + temporary pin for streaming latency regression

Team —

Quick ask from product: Polaris (external partner) has submitted the Polaris-XS 6B variant for production onboarding. Initial perf in our staging runs looks great for throughput, but we saw a consistent ~15–25ms regression on streaming tail latency vs. our current Aurora-6b baseline at 1024 token sequences. Because this customer is streaming-sensitive (live transcription use case), product is requesting a temporary version pin for Polaris-XS while we validate kernel/kv-cache behavior and collect 48h of canary telemetry.

Can we get alignment on the following by EOD?
- Engineering: confirm whether the latency regression is from tokenization/attention kernel choices or from KV cache priming.
- Runtime: feasibility of applying a targeted kernel switch or micro-quant profile to recover tail latency without blocking intake.
- SRE/Telem: proposed canary plan + telemetry windows we need to validate (p95/p99, payload distribution).

I've attached Polaris' inference spec and our initial latency comparison CSV. Sophie is on CC and can answer Polaris-specific questions. If we need an exception/access path to pin Polaris-XS in Dedicated for 48–72h, I want to document the reason and rollback criteria.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: polaris_inference_spec.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
[Attachment: polaris-latency-compare.csv (CSV, 8KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@polaris.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding Polaris-XS variant + temporary pin for streaming latency regression

Marcus —

Thanks for the heads-up and the artifacts. High-level findings from a quick look:
- The model uses a custom rotary embedding config that increases compute per-step slightly; that alone shouldn't explain p99 regressions.
- The KV cache access pattern in our staging traces shows more cache churn for sequences with many short turns (their streaming test has ~8 rapid partials per request). That could increase scheduling jitter.

Questions:
1) Are we pinning a specific model build (hash) or the Polaris-XS family? We should prefer pin-by-hash for rollback clarity.
2) What are the exact rollback criteria — is it absolute p99 latency threshold or relative to Aurora baseline?

From an engineering standpoint, if we pin by build hash we can gate traffic at the routing layer and enable a fast rollback path. If the fix is runtime-level, we may need a micro-kernel tweak which will require a short rebuild and a rolling deploy.

I can run a targeted profiling pass today if you confirm pin scope.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-canary-plan.md (MD, 4KB)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding Polaris-XS variant + temporary pin for streaming latency regression

Quick technical notes —
- I replayed their staging traces against two kernel configs: (A) default fused-attn kernels + per-layer fp16, (B) alternate tiled-attn kernels + micro-quant profile. Config B reduces average token compute by ~8% but adds a scheduling step that increased tail jitter on some microbenchmarks.
- The p99 jump looks correlated with small-batch scheduling on our multi-tenant pods when KV cache is being reallocated; the pattern matches their rapid partial-turn workload.

Actionable suggestions:
1) Pin by build-hash for 48 hours in Dedicated pool so we can run an isolated canary (no noisy neighbors).
2) While pinned, test kernel variant B on a mirror canary cluster with the same request distribution and enable prefix/KV warmup hooks for streaming sessions.
3) If kernel B reduces p99 by >=10% vs. current staging policy, we can enable it as a runtime knob for Polaris routes only.

I don't think we need a full rebuild to test — kernel switching at runtime is supported for this model family. I will coordinate with infra to configure a mirror canary today if we get approval.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Runtime Engineer, Inference Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@polaris.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 12:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding Polaris-XS variant + temporary pin for streaming latency regression

Hi Marcus / Laura / Dev —

Thanks for pulling this together so quickly. A few clarifications from our side:
- Polaris-XS build hash: polaris_xs_v1.3-20270828 (we can provide the exact artifact SHA on request).
- Their streaming load sim uses 90% short partials (50–200 tokens) with an average inter-part gap of ~350ms.
- Rollback criteria: Polaris asks that we only pin for the minimal time needed to verify no regression in p99 across their production-like trace; they're OK with 48–72h pin if the canary runs in isolation.

We're happy to provide additional traces or a curated prompt set to speed validation. We prefer pin-by-hash so our deploy automation can detect the exact artifact in your routing table.

—Sophie
Sophie Lam
Technical Partnerships, Polaris AI
[Attachment: polaris-streaming-trace-20270828.json (LOG, 2.1MB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Sophie Lam <sophie.lam@polaris.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding Polaris-XS variant + temporary pin for streaming latency regression

Thanks everyone — summary + asks:
- Decision: proceed with pin-by-hash (polaris_xs_v1.3-20270828) in Dedicated for a 48h isolated canary.
- Dev: please provision mirror canary with kernel variant B and enable KV warmup hooks; run against Sophie's trace set and our internal p95/p99 dashboards.
- Laura: run the profiling pass and document any micro-rebuild needs (if switching kernels introduces functional diffs).
- Priyom: please prepare routing rule and a rollback playbook (route cutover + immediate unpin) and ensure bookkeeping in MOD-4123.

Rollback criteria (agreed tentative): unpin if p99 for Polaris route exceeds Aurora baseline by >5% for two consecutive 30-min windows or if error rate increases >0.5% absolute. If canary shows improvement >=10% p99 reduction, we'll expand to a staged rollout.

Timeline: start canary tonight 21:00 PT. I'll update MOD-4123 with run results + decision.

Appreciate the fast turn — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
